summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 18% to Rs 202 crore and PAT 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore; FY27 target Rs 300 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue up about 18% to Rs 202 crore, EBITDA up 20% to Rs 37.39 crore with margin expansion, and PAT up 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore. Q4 revenue was described by an analyst as down about Rs 67 crore YoY, which management attributed to customer site readiness delaying dispatches and an LPG/gas supply disruption that hit fabrication plants. RDSO approval for cast wagon bogies is in hand, with capacity of 200-250 bogies a month built and first orders expected within about a month. FY27 is guided at Rs 300 crore, with a longer-term Rs 500 crore FY28 ambition.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 PAT margin (analyst's computation, not confirmed by management)

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 150 crore pending on book, of which about Rs 35-40 crore from BHEL

segments.name: Railways (cast and fabricated bogies)
segments.commentary: RDSO approval obtained to restart wagon bogies; capacity of 200-250 bogies a month, about 100-125 wagons. Casted bogie sale value about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Fabricated loco bogie developmental order in hand; about 50% of second preferential issue earmarked for fabricated bogie facilities.

segments.name: Steel (incl. coke oven doors)
segments.commentary: Orders from SMS and Thyssen for SAIL stamp-charging coke oven batteries; management claims about 70% share of coke oven doors made in India. Segment estimated at about Rs 50-60 crore of the Rs 200-220 crore revenue base.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Work for BHEL (since 1984-85) and L&T on 32 and 16 coal-based thermal plants to be commissioned by 2032; FY27 power revenue target about Rs 50 crore.

segments.name: Defence and shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Supplies A-brackets, B-brackets and stern boss castings to shipyards; Dhanush gun carriage components for GCF Jabalpur as one of several sources. Management says margins above 10%, but segment is 15-20% of revenue and not a current focus.

segments.name: Non-ferrous and other
segments.commentary: Castings for Hindalco, Vedanta (BALCO, HZL) and others; butterfly valve, pump, gearbox and machine tool castings. Management frames FY28 mix as 40% steel, 40% railways and power, and 20% other.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target Rs 300 crore: Rs 200 crore from existing business (already secured per management), Rs 50 crore from cast railway business and Rs 50 crore from power.
FY27 EBITDA/PAT margins guided similar to FY26; cost-side improvement visible in Q3-Q4 FY27.
FY28 ambition of Rs 500 crore, contingent on execution of Rs 300 crore this year, EPC orders, acquisitions and railway orders.
Long-term growth guidance of 45-50% CAGR reconfirmed when asked; margin floor stated as 8-10% minimum.
FY27 capex target about Rs 25 crore, unchanged from original plan.
Expect 100-200 bogie order within about a month and consistent 200 bogies a month production from September onwards.
capex_capacity: Cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month completed; equipment trials done, capitalisation pending prototype and first order (kept in CWIP until commercial production).
Fabricated bogie facility to be developed using about 50% of the second preferential issue (proposed Rs 50 crore: Rs 25 crore capital, Rs 25 crore working capital).
FY27 capex target about Rs 25 crore; FY26 capex about Rs 15 crore.
Centrifugal roll project (Rs 1.5-2 crore) dropped after market survey.
Spare land available at both Bhilai and Rajnandgaon units for expansion and semi-mechanisation.
demand_pricing: Bogie market split: about 70-75% wagon manufacturers and 20-25% railway spares directly; Texmaco and Titagarh outsource about 20-30% of bogie needs.
Industry bogie demand from an 8,000-10,000 wagon order cited at about 6,000 bogies (about 6,000 tonnes of castings).
Coke oven doors: India estimated at 150-180 batteries; replacement demand about 3-4% a year; order flow of 2-3 batteries a year, with 70-80 more batteries expected from planned capacity additions.
Q4 revenue shortfall attributed to customer site delays and LPG/gas availability constraints on fabrication plants; management said finished goods inventory was realised in April-May.
Labour sourcing from UP, Bihar, Bengal and Odisha is becoming harder as those states grow; company plans to skill local workers and add mechanisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is bogie capacity, and do wagon makers or Indian Railways buy bogies?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity 200-250 bogies a month (100-125 wagons). Customers are wagon manufacturers (70-75%) and railways directly for spares (20-25%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue fall YoY and why did margins rise to about 11% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited finished-goods inventory that could not be dispatched due to customer site conditions and an LPG shortage; margin target remains a minimum of 8-10%, driven by a strong demand environment and selective order intake.

qa_highlights.question: When will bogie orders arrive and is capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Discussions for 100-200 bogies; order expected in about a month. No further capex needed for cast bogies; equipment is in place and in CWIP.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue targets, margins, acquisitions and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 300 crore (Rs 200 crore existing, Rs 50 crore railways, Rs 50 crore power); margins similar; two acquisition leads open, one failed; FY27 capex Rs 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the centrifugal roll plan dropped, and what is the coke oven door opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Roll plan dropped as customers are served by Western and Eastern competitors and Jindal captive capacity. Coke oven doors: about 70% India share claimed, Rs 23 crore for one battery order from SMS; segment about Rs 50-60 crore, expected to reach about Rs 100 crore in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the Rs 500 crore FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution is the main risk; EPC, acquisitions and railway orders are the other pillars. Railways contribute about 30-40% of repetitive production bookings; acquisitions to be sought outside India on sensible PE multiples.

risks_watch: Execution risk: labour availability, gas/LPG supply, steel volatility and customer site readiness all affected Q4 dispatches.
Working-capital and funding need for fabricated bogies (proposed Rs 50 crore second preferential, debt or equity still undecided).
Bogie order flow depends on RDSO-qualified orders and the anticipated large wagon tender; no order yet confirmed.
Acquisition pipeline uncertain: one target failed on valuation, two open, size indicated as Rs 20-100 crore.
Q4 revenue decline YoY (per analyst, about Rs 67 crore) and inventory build-up to be verified in Q1 FY27 dispatches.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term pipeline (railways, steel, power) and margin floor, but guarded on Q4 execution, with the company attributing shortfalls to customer and gas-supply issues. Answers on FY28 targets and funding were open-ended.
key_quotes: We have achieved a robust double digit growth across all key parameters while significantly strengthening our balance sheet.
At least 70% of coke oven doors are being made at Simplex Castings.

adds.what: Cast bogie capacity of 200-250 bogies a month (about 100-125 wagons), equipment trials done, capitalisation pending prototype and first order

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of Rs 300 crore (about 49% over FY26's ~Rs 202 crore) is backed by Rs 200 crore from the existing business, Rs 50 crore from cast railway bogies (200-250 bogies/month capacity, RDSO approval, first 100-200 bogie order expected within a month) and Rs 50 crore from power, but the railway and power parts depend on orders not yet booked.
